transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get the pre-overtime huddle started. We've got Assembly Cell 8 available for weekend production of 480 pump housings, using our standard weekend plan — one Saturday shift and one Sunday shift, each up to 8 hours, with two operators per shift. Before I lock down the roster and production controls, I need each of you — workforce coordination, maintenance, and quality — to report any constraints or issues that could affect the plan. Who wants to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I've got a constraint from the certification matrix. Saturday's Cell 8 roster must be Lina, who is setup-certified, and Sam, who is run-certified. Sunday's roster must be Ruth, who is setup-certified, and Omar, who is run-certified. I checked the matrix after the last training audit, but the updated roster hasn't been attached to the weekend work order yet.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I've got a maintenance constraint. During my morning walkaround inspection of Cell 8, I found that the conveyor servo requires a 90-minute preventive inspection between the Saturday and Sunday shifts. I recorded it in my maintenance notebook but haven't entered it in the electronic work order yet. This needs to be scheduled in the gap between shifts, so it won't eat into either shift's production time, but it does need to be locked into the plan.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I've got a quality constraint from the customer quality amendment I received by email. It requires 12 first-off units after the weekend setup, and 100% torque verification on the first 30 units after the maintenance restart — with quality signoff before the remaining units can be released. The signed amendment hasn't been linked to the order record yet, so we need to make sure it's attached before production controls are locked.
transcript.speaker: A4
